newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-NZ'S LOMU CLEARED TO BEGIN COMEBACK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NZ'S LOMU CLEARED TO BEGIN COMEBACK.

text.p: England beware! Powerhouse All Black Jonah Lomu was cleared on Friday to begin his rugby comeback and hopes to make New Zealand's tour to Britain at the end of the year.

The giant winger, whose four-try destruction of England in the 1995 World Cup semifinals made him rugby's biggest star, has been given the green light to resume training following an enforced absence from the game with a kidney disorder.
The New Zealand Rugby Football Union (NZRFU) said Lomu had completed a six-month course of chemotherapy to treat the rare kidney disease nephrotic syndrome, and his condition had stabilised.
Lomu will undergo a fitness assessment by the All Black medical team, who will prescribe a structured fitness programme to help with his full return to rugby.
No date has been set for Lomu's return and he will be required to remain on medication to consolidate his improved kidney function.
The NZRFU said none of the medications would adversely affect his physical performance or contravene drug testing regulations.
All Black coach John Hart said recently he hoped to have Lomu as a member of the All Blacks on their tour of England, Ireland and Wales later this year.
Lomu has declared it a personal goal.
